If I were doing a blog/diary style website I would use HTML5, CSS, PHP, and MySQL. If that is too difficult, WordPress is your best bet. Stick with a cheap host until you figure out what your needs are, I would start with GoDaddy to acquire a domain name, and buy into one of their Linux shared hosting products. If you get more serious you may decide to find a better hosting company at some point, but GoDaddy is a decent place to start, and it has built-in support for WordPress if you end up going that route.

Squarespace is easier to use, but will end up costing you more and giving you less flexibility in the long run. If you're serious about learning website design and development, stay away from Squarespace. Whatever you do, get a firm understanding of HTML and CSS first, those are vitally important to all websites.

Do you want to learn how to make websites, or do you just want a website? There's no need to learn if you don't want to, just sign up for a Wordpress account and it's free and ready to use. No need for any coding.

Easiest way to get started would be to setup WordPress somewhere and buy a theme from theme forest (15 bucks).

A lot of servers will 1 - click installs for WordPress. Digital ocean is my goto for servers these days, its about 5 bucks a month for the basic package . You'll need a domain to, that's about 10 a year.
